title: Adir Hu
description: Adir Hu ("Mighty is He"), the Passover Seder song, in Hebrew to its traditional tune as the Union Haggadah printed it in 1923, in four parts of our own: the three verses the Union Haggadah prints, which take their names for Hashem from across the hymn's eight stanzas. Each verse praises Hashem as mighty (then chosen, great and one; then righteous, holy and merciful) and asks Him to build His house soon, speedily, in our days: "Kel bene, Kel bene", Hashem, build. Bright and stately.

credits.words: traditional Hebrew hymn of the Passover Haggadah

licence.words: public domain: traditional, anonymous (in the Haggadah since the fifteenth century, as the Union Haggadah's notes say)
licence.tune: public domain: traditional, printed as 'Traditional' in the Union Haggadah (1923); the Jewish Encyclopedia (1901) traces it to a Haggadah of 1644
licence.source: melody and words from The Union Haggadah: Home Service for the Passover, revised edition (edited and published by the Central Conference of American Rabbis, copyright 1923; the music 'as edited by the Society of American Cantors'), p. 81, "Addir Hu", Chorus, Maestoso, 'Traditional', in C, 4/4, voice and piano; written here in C as printed, the piano part used only to check the chords (no arranger is named). The print gives three verses: 'Addir hu, addir hu, yivneh veso b'korov...', then 'Bohur hu, godol hu, yohid hu, (Refrain)' and 'Tzaddik hu, kodosh hu, rahum hu, (Refrain)'. Its tune has three bars for the opening names (as verses 2 and 3 fill them), so verse 1 sings 'adir hu' a third time. The words are the print's, respelled from its Ashkenazi transliteration in modern Israeli pronunciation (ch for the guttural, ' only where the shva has no note of its own ('b'ne veitcha'); where the print gives it a note ('b'-ko-rov', 'b'-yo-me-nu', 'el b'-ne') it is spelled e), syllable for syllable as the notes carry them. The tune cross-checked against the Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (Funk & Wagnalls, New York, 1901), p. 187, 'Addir Hu', example B (by F. L. Cohen, who died in 1934, set to the 'Rahum Hu, Shaddai Hu, Takkif Hu' verse: the same tune in its first, third and 'bim-he-rah' bars and its close, with variants elsewhere, the second name rising A-B-C and 'El b'neh' starting low), and Abraham Baer, Baal T'fillah, 3rd edition (Frankfurt am Main: J. Kauffmann), No. 771, p. 171 (Baer died in 1894; there the first verse names Hashem once, and footnotes repeat bars for the longer verses). Breaths written in for beginners: the second 'hu' and the second 'bim-hei-rah' each give up three quarters of a beat. Read from the scan at archive.org/details/unionhaggadahhom00unse (leaf n100); divine names in substituted forms (Hillel, 2026-11-11), the forms customary when singing outside prayer: Kel, where the print has El.
